newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Two Nigerian activists freed, another held.
newsitem.headline: Two Nigerian activists freed, another held.

text.p: At least two leading members of the Nigerian opposition have been freed from detention while another was arrested, activists and local papers said on Thursday.
Chima Ubani, a member of the Democratic Alternative pressure group was released on Wednesday night after being held since June 1995, Ayo Obe of the Civil Liberties Organisation told Reuters.

Local newspapers said secretary of the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO) group Ayo Opadokun, 50, was freed from a prison in the capital Abuja on Wednesday while Doyin Okupe, a member of NADECO was arrested in Lagos.

There was no official confirmation of Opadakun's release but he was quoted by the independent National Concord newspaper as saying in Abuja: "The deputy controller of prisons just called me to inform me that my release order has come."
"There may have been more releases, but it is the practice of the government not to say when they are releasing people. They just let them go," Obe said.
"As that is often in remote areas it is obviously of some concern what happens to people after their release," she added.

Opadokun was detained in October 1994 after the government crushed strikes and riots in southwestern Nigeria pressing for the release and installation as president of Moshood Abiola, who is widely believed to have won an annulled 1993 election.

In June Nigeria freed half a dozen detainees to coincide with its first meeting with the Commonwealth from which the West African country was suspended last November after the hanging of nine minority rights activists for murder.
Despite the recent releases, many people remain in detention, chiefly Abiola and several pro-democracy activists.
